column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah has pardoned for me my nation: their mistakes, their forgetfulness and what they are coerced into.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by Ibn Mājah, al-Bayhaqī and others.
Al-khaṭaʾ (“mistakes”): when one intends something by his act and it turns out to be other than what he intended.
Wa-l-nisyān (“and forgetfulness”): with kasrah on the nūn; the opposite of remembering.
“What they are coerced into”: what they are forced into against their will.

The sin is lifted from one who makes a mistake, one who forgets and one who is coerced; but the ruling is not lifted. So if he destroys something by mistake, or a deposit is lost by him through forgetfulness, he is liable.

Excepted from coercion are fornication and killing, which do not become permissible through coercion; and excepted from forgetfulness is that whose cause a person brought about himself, for he is sinful in doing it because of his negligence.
